It is a white or almost white powder. Freely soluble in water; practically insoluble in alcohol. Store in airtight con- tainers. USNF 26 (Lactose Monohydrate). It is a natural disaccharide, obtained from milk, which consists of one glucose and one ga- lactose moiety. It may be modified as to its physical characteris- tics, and may contain varying proportions of amorphous lactose. It is a white, free-flowing powder. Freely, but slowly soluble in water; practically insoluble in alcohol. Store in airtight contain- ers. Adverse Effects and Precautions Lactose intolerance occurs due to a deficiency of the intestinal enzyme lactase. Ingestion of lactose by pa- tients with lactase deficiency leads to a clinical syn- drome of abdominal pain, diarrhoea, distension, and flatulence; symptoms may also occur in persons with- out such a deficiency who have ingested excessive amounts of lactose. Lactose is contra-indicated in patients with galactosae- mia, the glucose-galactose malabsorption syndrome, or lactase deficiency. Lactose intolerance. Reviews of lactose intolerance.1-3 The capacity of the infant intestine to produce lactase, the enzyme responsible for digesting lactose, is retained into adulthood only by a minority of the world’s population, mostly in those of north European descent; in Africa and Asia more than 90% of the pop- ulation are lactase deficient.
